public_sources.relevance: Primary basis for anytime-valid bounded/Bernoulli mean monitoring via betting confidence sequences.

public_sources.title: Anytime-Valid Inference Under Outcome Delay: A Design-Based Approach
public_sources.relevance: Recent primary evidence that timing-dependent observation demands an explicit filtration rather than treating completed outcomes as an unbiased ordinary sample.

anytime_mismatch_monitor.iid_or_conditional_model: For mismatch indicator M_t in {0,1}, to test a bad-rate null H0: p>=epsilon0 with iid p or a stronger per-step conditional lower bound, choose a predictable r<epsilon0 and use e_t(1)=r/epsilon0, e_t(0)=(1-r)/(1-epsilon0). The product is a nonnegative supermartingale under the stated null. Inverting such tests yields an anytime-valid upper-bound mechanism inside its model.
anytime_mismatch_monitor.zero_mismatch_special_case: With r=0, every match multiplies wealth by 1/(1-epsilon0) and any mismatch sets that component to zero. Crossing 1/delta after n zero mismatches occurs at n>=log(delta)/log(1-epsilon0), exactly reproducing the zero-failure fixed-sample count while remaining safe to stop at the crossing under the stated sequential model.
anytime_mismatch_monitor.robust_mixture: Use a predeclared mixture over r values in [0,epsilon0) if occasional mismatches should not permanently kill the monitor. Mixtures preserve e-validity; weights cannot be retrofitted after seeing mismatch outcomes without paying for selection.
anytime_mismatch_monitor.degradation_alarm: A separate upper-tail e-process with betting alternative r>epsilon_alarm tests H0:p<=epsilon_alarm and can alarm on worsening mismatch. Admission evidence and degradation alarms target opposite nulls and should have explicit risk budgets/state-transition rules.
anytime_mismatch_monitor.limitation: Historical mismatch evidence cannot prove an arbitrary future per-request conditional upper bound. It is only transferable under a frozen runtime fingerprint plus stated stationarity/exchangeability or explicit covariate-stratified assumptions.

marginal_vs_conditional_counterexample.construction: Two known prelaunch strata share one aggregate conformance stream. Stratum A is 95% of conformance traffic with selected-vs-canonical mismatch epsilon_A=0; stratum B is 5% with epsilon_B=0.10. Aggregate mismatch rate is only 0.005.
marginal_vs_conditional_counterexample.failure: If future evaluation happens to use only stratum B, the selected-sign null can be as high as P(Y=+)=0.60 even though aggregate conformance supports epsilon≈0.005. A robust paired-sign factor built from p0=.505 is then invalid: with r=.75 its one-step expected factor at p=.60 is about 1.093, and the 50-step threshold-20 false-cross probability is about 0.237 in the worker-local exact calculation.
marginal_vs_conditional_counterexample.lesson: A global mismatch rate is not a conditional identity guarantee. Prompt family, length/regime, engine/version, hardware placement, parallel topology, batch/concurrency and deterministic-mode implementation can be validity strata if they influence mismatch.

stratified_admission_rule.prelaunch_stratum: Compute a stratum/fingerprint x_t before outcome/timing is seen using only frozen operational covariates.
stratified_admission_rule.required_bound: Fastest-selected evidence for that attempt may use p0_t=.5+epsilon_U(x_t) only if epsilon_U(x_t) is a defensible predictable upper bound for the exact certified stratum. If no such bound exists, fastest stochastic selection is disabled for statistical evidence.
stratified_admission_rule.factor: For predictable r_t>p0_t, use e_t(+)=r_t/p0_t and e_t(-)=(1-r_t)/(1-p0_t). Heterogeneous p0_t across attempts is allowed because validity is checked conditionally step by step.
stratified_admission_rule.hierarchy: Sparse strata may borrow engineering evidence hierarchically for diagnosis, but a pooled marginal estimate cannot be used as a smaller statistical upper bound unless the pooling model itself supplies a valid conditional guarantee. Unknown/new fingerprints fail closed to canonical-attempt inference.
stratified_admission_rule.drift: Any version/hardware/kernel/configuration drift creates a new or invalidated stratum; do not silently inherit the old epsilon bound.

finite_horizon_fixed_bet_optimization.setup: Assume a valid constant conditional epsilon upper bound and canonical q_good=.60. For each epsilon, p0=.5+epsilon and worst selected good p=.6-epsilon. Search a fixed likelihood-ratio betting target r to maximize exact threshold-20 crossing by N=50.
finite_horizon_fixed_bet_optimization.interpretation: As identity uncertainty consumes most of the effect margin, the hard-horizon optimum becomes increasingly aggressive and power approaches the false-positive scale. This reinforces the Delta-2epsilon separation rule; betting optimization cannot recover information erased by approximate identity.
finite_horizon_fixed_bet_optimization.scope: Grid optimization over one fixed r only; not a Bellman/mixture optimum and not charged for a separate calibration-failure budget.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Use an anytime-valid Bernoulli mismatch monitor if certification can be stopped/adapted online; repeated fixed-sample intervals are not automatically safe under optional stopping.
Never substitute a pooled mismatch rate for a conditional stratum bound when the serving/evaluation sequence can concentrate on a high-mismatch stratum.
The stratum key must be available before outcome/timing and must include every operational dimension known to affect deterministic equivalence; otherwise the bound is not predictably scoped.
Unknown or drifted fingerprints revert to canonical single-attempt evaluation, not to a permissive pooled epsilon.
Finite-horizon betting can optimize the remaining evidence but cannot compensate when epsilon approaches half the target effect margin.
scope_guards: The simple e-factors above are exact for Bernoulli mismatch under their stated iid/conditional-probability null; they do not prove stationarity of a serving system.
The A/B stratum counterexample is synthetic and adversarial, designed to falsify pooled-rate reasoning rather than estimate any real engine's mismatch behavior.
The fixed-r power table assumes a known valid epsilon bound and q_good=.60; other effects/horizons require re-optimization.
Stratification can explode sample needs. The rule is fail-closed when evidence is sparse, not an instruction to manufacture precise bounds from tiny strata.

frontier.action: Design a practical fingerprint hierarchy and conformance allocation policy that minimizes certification cost while keeping statistical upper bounds genuinely conditional enough for fastest hedging. Compare per-stratum exact bounds, conservative parent fallback and deterministic-by-construction runtime contracts.

Build a mixture/Bellman paired-sign e-process robust to epsilon uncertainty intervals [epsilon_L,epsilon_U] rather than plugging in a single point bound; compare hard-horizon power and unresolved rate.

Stress mismatch bursts and fingerprint changes over time with an anytime degradation e-process; quantify detection delay versus false alarm and determine when hedging must be automatically demoted to canonical attempts.

Investigate timing-aware inference under explicit calibrated P(+|latency,covariates) bounds, while keeping calibration data disjoint from candidate generation and charging model uncertainty into the e-process.

frontier.exact_next_action: Construct a fingerprint-hierarchical admission policy with conservative parent fallback and an automatic mismatch-degradation demotion rule; simulate bursty rare-stratum failures to compare certification cost, detection delay, and false-commit control against a global pooled epsilon gate.
